newsitem.title: FRANCE: France wants U.N. to reaffirm Iraqi sovereignty.
newsitem.headline: France wants U.N. to reaffirm Iraqi sovereignty.

text.p: France said on Thursday that the U.N. Security Council must reaffirm Iraq's sovereignty and territorial integrity in any resolution concerning Baghdad's offensive in the Kurdish area of northern Iraq.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman said consultations were proceeding at the United Nations "in the right direction" on a draft resolution. Paris planned to offer amendments "better reflecting our position".

"In particular, we would like confirmation of the Republic of Iraq's sovereignty and territorial integrity, which has been reaffirmed in several previous Security Council Resolutions," spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said.
France, one of five permanent members of the Security Council along with the United States, Russia, Britain and China, has a right to veto any decision by the top U.N. body.

Eager to resume business with Iraq after United Nations economic sanctions against Baghdad are lifted, Paris pointedly declined to voice support for U.S. missile strikes this week after Baghdad sent troops into northern Iraq to intervene in fighting between two Kurdish factions.
French officials also made it clear that Paris had not agreed in advance to President Bill Clinton's extension of a no-fly zone in southern Iraq northwards from the 32nd to the 33th parallel.

The no-fly zones in northern and southern Iraq were set up by the allies after a U.S.-led coalition involving France drove Iraqi invasion forces out of Kuwait in 1991, to protect Iraq's Kurds and other groups on Iraqi soil from attack by Baghdad.
